gap: No result ChatGPT got says which UGREEN NAS UPS goes with the DXP2800 it picks. UGREEN's compatibility page lists the US3000 as 'Only Support 2-4Bay Series' and the US2000 as 'Only Support DH Series'. A family that wants a UPS to protect Audiobookshelf's SQLite database, which the Audiobookshelf docs warn can corrupt, should therefore buy the US3000 for a DXP2800, not the US2000.
standout_why: Pages compared: audiobookshelf.org Docker docs (cited), calibre-web.com (cited), hub.docker.com advplyr/audiobookshelf (cited), racksandwatts best-NAS-for-homelab-2026 (cited), mariushosting ABS-on-UGREEN (cited), Synology DS425+/DS225+ data sheets and HIG (cited) and our own page. None of them pairs a UPS with any candidate. Racksandwatts already covers the Synology storage rules: DSM 7.3 allows third-party SATA HDDs and SSDs on 2025 Plus models, but M.2 pools must use drives on Synology's list (it says this for the DS925+), and the DS225+ maxes out at 6 GB of RAM. Synology's data sheets and HIG that ChatGPT cited probably carry the DS425+ M.2 and RAM part numbers. So the Synology findings below would barely stand out. The UPS pairing is new, but it doesn't change which NAS wins.
decides: It supports the DXP2800 pick and its add-on. Pair the DXP2800 with the US3000, and correct Dealectric's catalog line for ugreen-nas-ups-us2000-72w, which says 'for NASync 2-Bay and DH Models', against UGREEN's 'Only Support DH Series'. The findings also count against the DS425+ as an 'SSD for app data' build. Synology's spec page allows an M.2 storage pool only on Synology SNV3410/SNV5420 SSDs, at 400 GB or more. On both the DS225+ and DS425+ the only memory upgrade Synology lists is the D4NS01-4G, for a 6 GB total, and Synology withholds complete warranty and support if you fit other RAM. The DXP2800 ships with 8 GB.

findings.label: Supported NAS models
findings.note: The page text gives the series rule only, and its per-model table did not load. I'm counting the DXP2800 as part of the '2-4Bay Series' because it is a 2-bay NASync model; the page does not name it.

findings.label: Supported NAS models
findings.value: 'Only Support DH Series' (DH2300, DH4300 Plus), so not the DXP2800
findings.note: This contradicts Dealectric's catalog name for ugreen-nas-ups-us2000-72w ('for NASync 2-Bay and DH Models'). Check the product page before linking it from a DXP2800 pick.

findings.label: Audiobookshelf database location
findings.value: /config (SQLite) 'must be accessible directly on the same machine running the Audiobookshelf server' and not over the network; network access leads to 'database corruption'
findings.note: ChatGPT already cited this page. The docs set no location rule for /metadata beyond keeping it out of other mount points. The docs don't mention power loss; I'm citing them only as the reason a UPS is worth adding.

findings.label: M.2 slots: storage-pool SSDs allowed
findings.value: 2× M.2 2280 NVMe for cache or storage pool; pools require Synology-verified SNV3410-400G, SNV5420-400G, SNV5420-800G or SNV5420-1600G; M.2 not hot-swappable
findings.note: Maker spec page. So putting ABS/Calibre-Web app data on NVMe means buying a 400 GB+ Synology enterprise SSD.

findings.label: Capacity / endurance / warranty
findings.source_title: Synology Enterprise Series M.2 NVMe SSD

findings.label: RAM upgrade
findings.value: 2 GB DDR4 non-ECC onboard, 1 slot, max 6 GB (2 GB + 4 GB) with D4NS01-4G; non-Synology memory means Synology 'will not provide complete product warranty or technical support'
findings.note: Maker spec page, optional accessories and footnote.

findings.label: RAM upgrade
findings.value: 2 GB DDR4 non-ECC onboard, 1 slot, max 6 GB (2 GB + 4 GB) with D4NS01-4G; same non-Synology memory warranty/support caveat
findings.note: The spec page lists no M.2 slots for the DS225+.

findings.label: Drives Synology lists as compatible
findings.value: 3.5" HDD: HAT3300/HAT3310/HAT3320, HAT5300/HAT5310/HAT5320; 2.5" SSD: SAT5221/SAT5210; 'Synology only guarantees full functionality, reliability, and performance for compatible drives'
findings.note: The maker page lists only Synology drives. Racksandwatts says DSM 7.3 still allows third-party SATA HDDs and SSDs in new pools on 2025 Plus models (see next finding).

findings.label: Third-party drives under DSM 7.3
findings.value: Third-party HDDs and 2.5-inch SATA SSDs allowed in new pools on 2025 Plus models; new M.2 pools and SSD cache need drives on Synology's list
findings.source_title: Best NAS for a homelab (2026) | Racks and Watts
findings.note: This is a rival page that ChatGPT cited, specs checked 2026-10-25. I couldn't load Synology's own KB article, which rendered without its body.

findings.label: RAM slot
findings.value: One DDR5 SO-DIMM slot, shipped with 8 GB DDR5-4800, reached after removing two screws; 2 M.2 slots beside the drive bays; OS on soldered eMMC
findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP2800 NAS im Test (Igor's Lab, Tim Kutzner)
findings.note: Named reviewer, published 2024-05-08 and updated 2025-05-31. The review doesn't give a maximum RAM figure or the M.2 PCIe lanes.

findings.label: Calibre-Web Automated on network shares
findings.value: Supported with NETWORK_SHARE_MODE=true (off by default), which disables SQLite WAL on metadata.db and app.db and switches to polling; README says shares are 'still slower than local disks'
findings.note: Only matters if the library sits on another box. On a NAS running the container locally, keep the default.
